topic_coverage.quoted_user_text: Operator pain: every US-xxxx story currently runs the full canonical lifecycle (architecture, qa, verify-work, ...) even for a simple README update. Need work-kind classification so small items skip overhead.
Target: this its-magic repo (Cursor IDE) plus consumer repos installed via its-magic; CI/headless parity preserved via existing outer-driver fallback.
Pure Python stdlib scripts (scripts/*.py) plus markdown command files (.cursor/commands/*.md) plus scratchpad flags plus backlog/acceptance row fields. No new runtime.

Default-off additive WORK_KIND_ROUTING scratchpad flag; composes with US-0096 delivery modes, US-0070 phase selection, US-0078 intake evidence, US-0051 decomposition. Operator accept/override before write.
No GUI. Operator surface = backlog row fields (work_kind, recommended_delivery_mode) + state.md breadcrumb + intake-time accept/override prompt + CLI classifier self-test.
Standard its-magic hygiene only: no .env reads, no secret surface; classifier sees prose + touched-file hints (names-only); optional audit trail via US-0103 AI decision ledger.
Deterministic + fail-closed reason codes; zero overhead when WORK_KIND_ROUTING=0; explicit precedence vs DELIVERY_MODE and AUTO_PHASE_* (explicit operator flags win).
Single story, one vertical slice: classifier lib + scratchpad flag + intake integration + /auto integration + reason codes + tests + parity shipped together.
